A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research questions and central results. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite substantial figure reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network training simulations, channel-frequency measurements, perturbation experiments and optimizer trajectories in Figures 2–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and reports additional sharpness measurements, gradient-descent learning-rate experiments and a ReLU population-loss example.

M1.justification: The neuron-duplication, finite-difference reparameterization and jump procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 modifies the channel-identification heuristic: update alignment, previously a diagnostic, becomes an explicit acceptance condition using a revised channel-subspace projection.

E1.justification: v2 adds a two-dimensional regression example involving a discontinuous derivative-gated target and a ReLU network under population loss (Appendix B.4, Figure B13). The Rosenbrock, four Gaussian-process families and one-dimensional erf teacher–student task are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding optimizer-trajectory comparison retains finite- and infinite-data gradient flow, SGD and Adam (v1 Figure 6b; v2 Figure 6b). The added GD learning-rate sweep investigates stability without adding a competing baseline to that comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 substantially revises the central measurement protocol: the cosine-distance cutoff changes from 0.01 to 0.001, and channel identification requires over 90% of updates within a newly specified channel subspace. v2 also introduces GD learning-rate and ReLU population-loss experiments. Section 3 changes the reported auxiliary activation tests from tanh to sigmoid; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a learning-rate sensitivity analysis of optimizer stalling (Figure 6d), sharpness scaling along a channel (Figure 5), a landscape slice along the sharpest direction (Figure B12), and a ReLU case study (Figure B13). It also reworks the earlier parallel-update diagnostics into channel-subspace analyses.

E5.justification: The stated repetition counts remain 50 initializations per configuration in Appendix B.3 and 50 times 2^r simulations per architecture in Appendix A.2. Existing error-bar reporting is retained, with no new confidence-interval, significance-testing or seed-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Reported channel frequencies change from 52%, 34%, 40%, 73% and 80% in v1 Figure 5b to 24%, 20%, 30%, 61% and 64% in v2 Figure 4c, respectively for Rosenbrock and GP scales 0.1, 0.5, 2 and 10. These use revised identification rules and are not same-setting performance changes. v2 additionally reports sharpness scaling, learning-rate-dependent stability results and the ReLU example.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3.2 adds a closed-form derivation of Gaussian expectations for ReLU activations, culminating in Equation 28. Section 4 adds reasoning connecting sharpness scaling as 1/epsilon^2 to a step-size-dependent minimum epsilon. The setup also changes its activation assumption from differentiable to continuous, while retaining the earlier GLU, loss-expansion and higher-derivative derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same substantive claims: identifying channels to infinity, finding them frequently under gradient-based training, and interpreting their limiting functions as gated linear units. The additional analyses support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the tentative explanation of SGD/Adam stalling through small slopes and possible implicit regularization with a categorical edge-of-stability explanation. It adds finite-data cusp limitations for ReLU, interpretations involving architectural mismatch and regularization, and removes the speculative explanation of star-shaped connectivity.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository address, channel-subspace projection formulas, and the ReLU example's teacher weights and epsilon value. Table 1, hardware information, ODE settings and the existing SGD/Adam hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to Lim et al. on neural-network approximation and Chen et al. on stochastic collapse, plus Fischer et al. and another Owen reference for the ReLU derivation. Three implicit-regularization references are removed. The principal positioning around neuron splitting and loss-landscape geometry remains.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording, enumerates contributions and identification criteria, expands the geometric explanation, and reorganizes appendix subsections. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the preprint footer becomes a conference footer.

P2.justification: Material from v1 Figures 2 and 3 is consolidated into v2 Figure 2, with additional panels moved to Appendix Figure A2. v1 Figure 6 is split and expanded into v2 Figures 5 and 6. The channel-summary panels are rearranged and relabeled, and Figures B12–B13 add new visualizations.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's acknowledged potential channel misclassification with stricter screening, extends the population-loss analysis to ReLU, and adds useful sharpness and stability experiments. Code access information also improves reproducibility. These strengthen an already-supported central result, although the new stability experiment directly tests GD and does not fully establish the categorical SGD/Adam explanation in the revised prose.
